name: Fei Miao
title: Pratt & Whitney Associate Professor
department: School of Computing; Electrical and Computer Engineering courtesy appointment
fitReason: Strong control/learning foundation with newly verified physical imitation-learning and VLA manipulation, complementing the group's autonomous-vehicle and multi-agent work.

physicalEvidence.summary: May11,2026 SEVO tests ACT and SmolVLA policies on two real SO-101-arm platforms: a Jetson Orin NX custom mobile robot and a Raspberry Pi5 IKEA cart. Body-fixed cameras, red illumination, YOLO segmentation and diversified demonstrations support transparent-bottle pick-and-place. Only the arm is learned; base navigation is separate and stops before grasping. All three authors list UConn Computing and Miao is corresponding author. This is a controlled single-object task, not general household autonomy. SmolVLA is slow, and the paper's Raspberry-Pi ACT latency statements conflict; no real-time claim is adopted.

name: Lillian J. Ratliff
title: Associate Professor; Afroze and Sherali Dhanani Endowed Faculty Fellow
department: Electrical and Computer Engineering; adjunct Computer Science and Engineering; adjunct Aeronautics and Astronautics
fitReason: Direct fit for rigorous safe-learning methods and their physical humanoid deployment, with control, optimization and game-theoretic foundations.

physicalEvidence.summary: September18,2026 LIMBO synthesizes a learned Q-CBF and distills safety feedback into PPO residual policies, trained in simulation and deployed on a29-DoF Unitree G1. Physical tests include human-thrown balls tracked by motion capture and low-obstacle locomotion; scripted-ball hardware tests are distinguished from real throws. Human-throw hit-rate differences are not statistically significant. The paper notes work during an Amazon internship, so this is collaborative hardware evidence, not confirmed UW-owned equipment. UW independently identifies first author Jake Gonzales as Ratliff's coadvised doctoral student.
